pull.title: rpc: Use OBJ_NAMED_PARAMS in estimatesmartfee
pull.body:
`estimatesmartfee` is the only RPC that rejects named arguments for options, which seems confusing and not user friendly.

Fix it by using `OBJ_NAMED_PARAMS`.

comments.body:
> [fad1c43](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36976/changes/fad1c43ea15b8bf99c58bbde57958f4588ec6806) _test: Fix TestNodeCLI error msg parsing_:

`bitcoin-cli` always ends this output with a newline as far as I can tell, matching a required trailing `\n` outside the capture with `re.fullmatch` lets us drop `removesuffix` and `-?\d+` would also be simpler (and more correct since the old `[-0-9]+` also matches values like `-3-`).

<details>
<summary>Example patch</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/test_framework/test_node.py b/test/functional/test_framework/test_node.py
index 7abd78f560..f88a317061 100755
--- a/test/functional/test_framework/test_node.py
+++ b/test/functional/test_framework/test_node.py
@@ -1011,10 +1011,9 @@ class TestNodeCLI():
         cli_stdout, cli_stderr = process.communicate(input=stdin_data)
         returncode = process.poll()
         if returncode:
-            match = re.match(r'error code: ([-0-9]+)\nerror message:\n(.*)', cli_stderr, re.DOTALL)
+            match = re.fullmatch(r'error code: (-?\d+)\nerror message:\n(.*)\n', cli_stderr, re.DOTALL)
             if match:
                 code, message = match.groups()
-                message = message.removesuffix("\n")
                 raise JSONRPCException(dict(code=int(code), message=message))
             match = re.match(r'error: Server response: (.*)\n?$', cli_stderr)
             if match:
```

</details>

+def assert_rpc_options_validation(
+    rpc: Callable,
+    *,
+    reject_wrong_option_type: Optional[tuple[str, object]] = None,
+):
+    """Check common validation behavior for an RPC with an options object.
+
+    `rpc` should be a callable that accepts keyword arguments, typically a
+    lambda which supplies the RPC's required arguments.
+    Set `reject_wrong_option_type` to an (option name, value) pair to test that case.
+    """
+    assert_raises_rpc_error(-3, "Unexpected key unknown_option", rpc, options={"unknown_option": 1})
+    assert_raises_rpc_error(-8, "Unknown named parameter unknown_option", rpc, unknown_option=1)
+    assert_raises_rpc_error(-3, "type array is not of expected type object", rpc, options=[])
+    if reject_wrong_option_type:
+        key, val= reject_wrong_option_type

> [fa73731](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36976/changes/fa73731ceb9378b8c7111f72b3299c612ba888b5) _rpc: Use OBJ\_NAMED\_PARAMS in estimatesmartfee_:

Both values here are defaults. Using non-default values and checking the result would show that the named arguments actually select the estimator and enable the extra statistics.

<summary>Example patch</summary>

diff --git a/test/functional/rpc_estimatefee.py b/test/functional/rpc_estimatefee.py

 from test_framework.util import (
+    assert_equal,
     assert_raises_rpc_error,
     assert_rpc_options_validation,
 )
@@ -63,8 +64,12 @@ class EstimateFeeTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(1, 'unset')
         self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(1, 'conservative')
         self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(1, 'ECONOMICAL', {"fee_rate_estimator": "block_policy"})
-        self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(1, 'ECONOMICAL', {"fee_rate_estimator": "mempool_policy"})
-        self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(1, 'ECONOMICAL', verbosity=1, fee_rate_estimator="auto")
+
+        options = {"fee_rate_estimator": "mempool_policy", "verbosity": 2}
+        named = self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(conf_target=6, **options)
+        assert_equal(named, self.nodes[0].estimatesmartfee(6, 'ECONOMICAL', options))
+        assert_equal(named["blocks"], 2)
+        assert "mempool_health_statistics" in named
 
         self.nodes[0].estimaterawfee(1)
